text:
Alex: Heads-up — seeing a steady memory climb on long streaming sessions when tool loops hit ~2000 tokens. Not an instant OOM, just slow upward drift over hours.
Maria: Can you repro locally or is this only on staging/dedicated?
Alex: Staging + a couple prod-simdedicated runs. Repro rate ~60% on the 12h soak harness.
Chen: Did we rule out simple fragmentation vs retained refs in KV? Any refcount spikes?
Alex: refcounts look stable, but page residency keeps increasing. Heap top shows more 'kv_page' residency over time.
Sam: Can you paste the pmap/heap profile?
Alex: Pstack + pprof snippets below. Note: this is streaming-chat -> toolchain loop where each turn appends new prefix and we keep KV entries for tool outputs.
```
# pmap tail
00007f9c8c000-00007f9c90000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0  [anon:kv_page_pool]
00007f9c90000-00007f9c98000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0  [anon:kv_page_pool:partial]
# pprof top
1.5GB  30%  kv_page_alloc
0.8GB  16%  kv_page_retained
0.3GB   6%  batching::prefetch_worker
```
Chen: Interesting. The allocator accounts show lots of partially filled slabs. Could be we aren't returning pages when eviction policy deems them cold because longchain pinned sequences keep occasional hits.
Riley: Do we have a timeline of when kernel selection/batching changes rolled? We touched L2 kernel choices last week. Could overlap.
Maria: I pulled an old trace from before the L2 kernel change. Comparing profiles now.
Chen: If kernel selection altered per-token latency distribution, batching heuristics might change minibatch sizes, affecting KV churn and prefix caching pressure. Worth correlating.
Sam: Any logs showing eviction decisions? We added extra logging for evict decisions behind --kv-evict-log but it's noisy.
Alex: I captured a short trace with evict logging. Key bits: the evict pass marks pages as reclaimable but some are re-pinned in the same sweep by tool loop reads. Reclaim counter increments but physical pages remain mapped.
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:01Z] evict: candidate page=0x7f9c8c001000 age=3600 access_count=1
[2026-03-17T03:12:01Z] reclaim: candidate page=0x7f9c8c001000 -> bounce to hot pool
[2026-03-17T03:12:01Z] page_pin: toolloop read id=4789 page=0x7f9c8c001000
```
Maria: So pages flagged cold then immediately re-pinned — suggests our eviction TTL is too aggressive or our access heuristics are too coarse.
Chen: Or a race: evict sweeper marks candidate, then concurrent read sees the page and increments holdcount before the free path completes, preventing actual release. We had a fix for holdcount atomic ordering in 2025-11 but maybe reverted?
Riley: I recall a revert around kernel-selection PR where some allocator fencing got simplified. Ping @infra-bot for recent revert list.
infra-bot: Revert log for last 30 days: 2026-02-28 vm/kv-alloc-fence revert, 2026-03-05 kernel-l2-sel tweak (non-fatal), 2026-03-09 batching/heuristics simplification.
Alex: vm/kv-alloc-fence revert is suspicious. That fence prevented concurrent pin after candidate selection.
Sam: Reintroducing that fence might reduce throughput slightly — need to measure. But correctness > perf here.
Chen: Quick experiment idea: instrument eviction to delay marking reclaimable by 50ms and see if net release happens. If re-pins are within that window, we'll see higher retention without change.
Alex: Ran that on staging for 6h. Memory plateaued instead of climbing. So this supports racing re-pins.
Maria: Nice. Can you share the patch?
Alex: Patch is small, toggled via --kv-evict-defer-ms=50. Code snippet: 
```
// before marking candidate reclaimable
if (defer_ms > 0) sleep_ms(defer_ms);
mark_reclaimable(page);
```
Riley: That's a pragmatic probe but sleeping in sweeper thread may hurt steady-state latency. Better to schedule deferred mark via timer wheel.
Chen: Agreed. Also need to confirm we don't create pathological backlog if many pages pile up. Run sustained 24h with high concurrency.
Sam: Also measure token throughput and p99 latency. We should add an AB test toggled at route level.
Alex: Results from 6h test: memory growth flat, CPU +1.8%, p99 latency +5% in worst windows. Throughput unchanged.
Maria: For next steps: (1) reintroduce fence as hotfix on Dedicated and staging, (2) implement defer via async mark + timer wheel for mainline, (3) add longer soak + AB.
Chen: I'll volunteer to spec the timer-wheel approach and run the 24h soak on a dedicated pool.
Riley: I'll open an infra ticket to track the vm/kv-alloc-fence revert and link this thread.
Sam: Also add an eval to the perf regression dashboard to look for kernel-selection churn correlation.
Alex: Filed issue RFC-4821 with links and the staging logs. Tagged the PR as WIP: //pr/infra/kv-evict-defer.
Maria: Thanks. Great triage — feels like a race between evict and toolloop pin.
Chen: One more note: double-check GC of ephemeral tool outputs. If we accidentally keep references in the work queue for longer, that will amplify re-pins.
Alex: Agreed. I'll grep for queue lifetimes and run a tight repro with artificial high-repin frequency.
Riley: Next sync? Let's reconvene after the 24h soak. :calendar:
Alex: SGTM. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
